subject: Re: Geo surcharge credit offset & channel margin alignment for Azure private offer
messages:
From: Simone Park <simone.park@edgecloud.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeCloud Procurement <procure@edgecloud.com>
Date: 2027-12-19T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private offer: regional surcharge and reseller crediting question

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving to finalize the Azure private offer for our EU nodes but hit a wrinkle on the list-price delta for the UK/IE regions. Our finance team applies a 6% regional surcharge on top of list price (local taxes aside) and they expect that surcharge to be absorbed or offset by channel credits in the private offer.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a recommended routing for a surcharge offset so EdgeCloud doesn't double-bill customers (we'd prefer an offset applied at invoice/crediting rather than changing public list prices)?
- Second, we need clarity on how reseller commissions would be calculated if we apply an offset: does Redwood treat the private-offer net revenue as the commission base or the pre-offset list price?

Procurement is pushed on timing (they want PO issued before year-end). I can loop in our procurement contact (cc'ed).

Appreciate any quick guidance — Simone
Simone Park
Head of Partnerships, EdgeCloud
phone: +44 20 7946 0210

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Simone Park <simone.park@edgecloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-19T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: regional surcharge and reseller crediting question

Hi Simone —

Thanks for the clear summary. Short version up front: we can support an invoice-level surcharge offset so your customers don't see a different public list price, and we recommend calculating commissions on post-offset net revenue for reseller payout, but there are two operational patterns with different accounting impacts:

1) Marketplace crediting (preferred for clean invoicing): Redwood issues a negative line ("Regional surcharge credit") in the private-offer settlement that matches the surcharge amount. EdgeCloud invoices full list price to the customer; Redwood's private-offer settlement nets out the surcharge. Commission is paid on the net settlement amount. Pros: transparent to customer; Cons: requires settlement/reconciliation cadence alignment.

2) List-price adjustment (rare): Redwood publishes a region-specific list-price variant for the private offer. Commission calculations remain consistent relative to the listed price per invoice, but this requires catalog changes and SKU mapping in the marketplace — slower to implement.

Attached is a quick model (channel_margin_offset_v2.xlsx) showing both flows and the impact on reseller margin at typical commission rates (15% and 20%). Ben, can you validate the commission calculation if we treat the private-offer settlement as the commission base? Irene, any ops constraints for issuing the negative settlement line in Azure private offer?

Next step suggestion: if procurement needs PO now, we can sign a term sheet that commits to the settlement workflow above and follow up with the exact settlement cadence and invoice reference fields. I can draft language for the PO to reduce back-and-forth.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Simone Park <simone.park@edgecloud.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-20T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: regional surcharge and reseller crediting question

Thanks Grace. Quick verification from the commission ops side:

- If Redwood issues a settlement credit line to offset the surcharge, we calculate reseller commission on the settlement net (post-offset). Example: List price 1000 EUR + surcharge 60 EUR. Settlement to EdgeCloud becomes 1000 EUR (customer pays 1060 EUR but Redwood nets 60 EUR as a credit) -> Commission base = 1000 EUR.
- If EdgeCloud prefers to keep commission tied to the pre-offset list price (i.e., commission on 1060 EUR), we can do that but it requires an explicit override and will increase total commission payout and affect Redwood revenue recognition; we'd need legal sign-off.

Irene — operational ask: we'll need EdgeCloud to include a consistent invoice reference field so our settlement system can auto-match the surcharge credit against the invoice. If procurement can include the field "Redwood PO ID" on the invoice, that will speed reconciliation.

Simone — I've attached a sample clause below that we typically add to the private offer terms to lock in the chosen treatment. If you agree, Grace and I can push the clause into the DocuSign term sheet and get signatures.

Sample clause (draft):
"For regional list-price differentials ("Surcharge"), Redwood will apply a settlement credit against the private offer such that the Marketplace settlement to the Reseller (EdgeCloud) reflects the published list price net of any Surcharge. Commissions will be calculated on the resultant settlement amount unless otherwise agreed in writing."

Ben Carter
Senior Account Director | Redwood Inference

From: Simone Park <simone.park@edgecloud.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeCloud Procurement <procure@edgecloud.com>
Date: 2027-12-21T14:36:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: regional surcharge and reseller crediting question

Hi Grace / Ben —

This alignment works for us. Procurement just needs the clause in the PO and confirmation on two items before we can issue:
1) Confirmation that settlement credits will be visible on monthly statements with invoice refs for auto-reconciliation.
2) Lead time to set up the negative settlement line in Azure private offer (we need to know if this is a <=10 business day change or if it will stretch to multiple weeks).

Attached is our PO terms (EdgeCloud_PO_terms.pdf) for your review — it's lightweight. If Redwood can confirm (1) and (2) we will sign and issue PO by EOD next Thursday. DocuSign link: https://docuSign.com/link/to/azure-private-offer

Thanks — Simone
